name: Tambda Rassa
blurb: Kolhapur's fiery red mutton broth, drunk on the side or poured over rice.

steps.text: Pressure cook the mutton with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, salt and five cups of water. Keep the stock.
Roast the coconut, sesame, chillies and one onion; grind to a paste.
Fry the whole spices and the other onion; add the paste and Kolhapuri masala and fry until the oil leaves.
Pour in the stock and mutton; simmer until thin and red.
Finish with coriander.

name: Malvani Chicken
blurb: Konkan-coast chicken curry with roasted coconut and Malvani masala.

steps.text: Roast the coconut, coriander seeds, pepper and one onion until brown; grind with water.
Sear the chicken with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric and Malvani masala.
Add the other onion, chopped, and the tomato; cook down.
Add the coconut paste and water; simmer until the chicken is done.
Finish with coriander.

name: Masale Bhat
blurb: Maharashtrian spiced rice with ivy gourd or brinjal and goda masala, served at weddings.

steps.text: Soak the rice for 30 minutes.
Crackle the mustard, cumin, hing and curry leaves; add the cashews and vegetables.
Add turmeric, goda masala and the rice; stir two minutes.
Add three cups of hot water and salt. Cover and cook on low until done.
Top with coconut and coriander.

name: Pithla Bhakri
blurb: Thick, spiced besan porridge with jowar flatbreads. A farmhouse meal from Maharashtra.

steps.text: Knead the jowar flour with hot water and pat out bhakris by hand; cook each on a hot tawa, both sides.
Whisk the besan into three cups of water with turmeric and salt until smooth.
Crackle the mustard, cumin, hing and curry leaves; fry the garlic, chillies and onion.
Pour in the besan and stir on low until it thickens.
Finish with coriander and serve with the bhakris.

name: Matki Usal
blurb: Sprouted moth beans in a coconut and goda masala gravy. Sprout them a day ahead.

steps.text: Soak the matki overnight, drain and keep covered until sprouted.
Crackle the mustard, hing and curry leaves; soften the onion and ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder, goda masala and coconut; cook down.
Add the sprouts and a cup of water; cook covered until tender.
Finish with coriander.

name: Prawn Balchao
blurb: Goa's hot and sour prawn pickle-curry with dried chillies and vinegar.

steps.text: Soak the chillies, cumin, pepper, cinnamon and cloves in the vinegar and grind with the garlic and ginger.
Fry the prawns with salt and turmeric until just pink. Set aside.
Brown the onions, add the tomato and the paste and fry until the oil leaves.
Add the prawns and sugar; cook three minutes. It keeps for days in the fridge.

name: Chicken Cafreal
blurb: Goan chicken in a green paste of coriander, chillies and spices, pan-roasted until dry.

steps.text: Grind the coriander, chillies, garlic, ginger, whole spices, turmeric and lemon to a smooth green paste.
Coat the chicken in it with salt and leave for an hour.
Sear the chicken in oil, then cover and cook in its own juices until done.
Uncover and roast until the masala clings.

name: Sorpotel
blurb: Goa's pork curry with vinegar and dried chillies. Better on day two or three.

steps.text: Boil the pork until just cooked, cool and dice it small. Keep the stock.
Grind the chillies, whole spices, turmeric, garlic and ginger with the vinegar.
Fry the onions and chillies, add the paste and fry well, then the pork.
Add some stock and simmer until thick. Rest it overnight before serving.

name: Musur Dal
blurb: Bengali red lentil dal, thin and light, with a tempering of kalonji and dried chilli.

steps.text: Boil the dal with turmeric in four cups of water until it breaks down.
Heat the mustard oil, add kalonji, dried chillies and green chillies, then the onion until golden.
Add the tomato, then the dal and salt; simmer five minutes.
Finish with coriander.

name: Cholar Dal
blurb: Sweet and savoury Bengal gram dal with coconut, raisins and whole spices. Made with luchi.

steps.text: Soak the dal for an hour and cook it with turmeric until soft but whole.
Heat the ghee; add cumin, bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom and coconut; fry until light brown.
Add grated ginger, chillies, the dal, raisins, sugar and salt.
Simmer until thick.

name: Aloo Posto
blurb: Potatoes in a paste of poppy seeds and green chilli. Bengal's simplest comfort food.

steps.text: Soak the poppy seeds for 30 minutes and grind them with two chillies to a paste.
Heat mustard oil, add kalonji and a slit chilli, then the cubed potatoes, turmeric and salt.
Add the poppy paste and half a cup of water. Cover and cook until the potatoes are soft.
Drizzle a little raw mustard oil on top.

name: Shukto
blurb: A mild, faintly bitter mixed-vegetable stew that starts a Bengali meal.

ingredients.label: Mixed vegetables (raw banana, sweet potato, brinjal, drumstick)

steps.text: Grind the mustard and poppy seeds to a paste.
Fry the sliced bitter gourd in mustard oil until crisp. Set aside.
Fry panch phoron and the bay leaf; add the vegetables and cook covered.
Add the paste, milk, dry ginger, sugar and salt; simmer until tender.
Add the bitter gourd back and finish with ghee.

name: Doi Maach
blurb: Fish in a gently spiced yogurt gravy with whole garam masala.

steps.text: Rub the fish with salt and turmeric and fry it lightly in mustard oil.
Fry the whole spices and bay leaves; add the onion and ginger paste until golden.
Whisk the yogurt with chilli powder and sugar, lower the heat and stir it in.
Slide in the fish and simmer five minutes.

name: Chicken Rezala
blurb: Kolkata's white chicken curry with yogurt, cashews and poppy seeds.

steps.text: Soak the cashews and poppy seeds and grind them with one onion to a smooth paste.
Marinate the chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste and white pepper for 30 minutes.
Fry the whole spices and chillies in ghee; add the paste and cook gently without browning.
Add the chicken and cook covered until done.
Finish with nutmeg, kewra and sugar.

name: Dal Dhokli
blurb: Spiced wheat dough pieces simmered in sweet and sour Gujarati toor dal.

steps.text: Cook the dal soft and whisk it smooth.
Knead the atta, besan, ajwain, oil, half the turmeric and chilli into a firm dough; roll thin and cut diamonds.
Bring the dal to a boil with four cups of water, the tomato, peanuts, kokum, jaggery and salt.
Drop in the dough pieces and simmer until cooked through.
Temper the mustard, cloves and curry leaves in ghee and pour over. Finish with coriander.

name: Gujarati Kadhi
blurb: Thin, sweet and gently spiced yogurt kadhi without pakoras. Eaten with khichdi.

steps.text: Whisk the yogurt, besan, three cups of water, ginger, chillies, sugar and salt until smooth.
Bring it to a boil, stirring, and simmer until it no longer tastes raw.
Temper the mustard, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, fenugreek, hing and curry leaves in ghee; pour over.
Finish with coriander.

name: Sev Tameta Nu Shaak
blurb: Tomatoes cooked sweet-sour and topped with crisp sev at the table. Kathiawad's fast curry.

steps.text: Crackle the mustard, cumin and hing; add the chopped tomatoes.
Add the spices, salt and jaggery; cook until soft and saucy.
Add half a cup of water and simmer two minutes.
Top with sev and coriander just before eating, so the sev stays crisp.

name: Ringan No Olo
blurb: Gujarati fire-roasted brinjal mash with garlic and spring onion.

steps.text: Roast the brinjal over a flame until black and soft; peel and mash.
Fry the cumin, crushed garlic and chillies; add the spring onions.
Add the tomato and spices; cook until soft.
Stir in the brinjal and cook five minutes.

name: Dhansak
blurb: The Parsi Sunday dish: mutton cooked into lentils and vegetables, with caramelised brown rice.

steps.text: Soak the dals for an hour, then pressure cook them with the vegetables, methi and turmeric; blend smooth.
Brown two onions, add ginger-garlic paste, the mutton, chilli powder and garam masala; cook until tender.
Combine the mutton with the dal and simmer.
For the rice: caramelise the sugar in oil, add the whole spices, one sliced onion, the rice and water; cook until done.

name: Ker Sangri
blurb: Desert berries and beans dried in the sun, cooked with spices. Rajasthan's travelling vegetable.

steps.text: Soak the ker and sangri overnight, then boil them until soft and drain.
Heat mustard oil, crackle the cumin and hing.
Add the spices with a splash of water, then the ker sangri, raisins and yogurt.
Cook on low until dry and coated, then add the amchur.
